requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding WKS RDATA.
requirements.required_behavior: Place ADDRESS first, PROTOCOL immediately after ADDRESS, and the BIT MAP after PROTOCOL.
requirements.why_checkable: The WKS wire layout can be checked for the specified field sequence.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the ADDRESS field of WKS RDATA.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent ADDRESS as a 32-bit Internet address.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and address interpretation can be checked in the WKS codec.

requirements.quote: PROTOCOL        An 8 bit IP protocol number
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the PROTOCOL field of WKS RDATA.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent PROTOCOL as an 8-bit IP protocol number.
requirements.why_checkable: The protocol field width and numeric interpretation are directly inspectable.

<BIT MAP>       A variable length bit map.  The bit map must be a
                multiple of 8 bits long.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a WKS service bitmap.
requirements.why_checkable: WKS records with different whole-octet bitmap lengths can exercise variable-length handling.

requirements.quote:
<BIT MAP>       A variable length bit map.  The bit map must be a
                multiple of 8 bits long.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the bitmap length a multiple of 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The number of encoded bitmap bits can be checked for octet alignment.

requirements.quote:
The WKS record is used to describe the well known services supported by
a particular protocol on a particular internet address.  The PROTOCOL
field specifies an IP protocol number, and the bit map has one bit per
port of the specified protocol.  The first bit corresponds to port 0,
the second to port 1, etc.  If the bit map does not include a bit for a
protocol of interest, that bit is assumed zero.  The appropriate values
and mnemonics for ports and protocols are specified in [RFC-1010].
requirements.condition: When interpreting the bitmap in a WKS record.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret its port bits in the IP protocol selected by the PROTOCOL field.
requirements.why_checkable: The same bitmap can be decoded under different protocol values to check the cross-field association.

requirements.quote:
The WKS record is used to describe the well known services supported by
a particular protocol on a particular internet address.  The PROTOCOL
field specifies an IP protocol number, and the bit map has one bit per
port of the specified protocol.  The first bit corresponds to port 0,
the second to port 1, etc.  If the bit map does not include a bit for a
protocol of interest, that bit is assumed zero.  The appropriate values
and mnemonics for ports and protocols are specified in [RFC-1010].

For example, if PROTOCOL=TCP (6), the 26th bit corresponds to TCP port
25 (SMTP).  If this bit is set, a SMTP server should be listening on TCP
port 25; if zero, SMTP service is not supported on the specified
address.
requirements.condition: When advertising a service with a set WKS bitmap bit.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the set bit to indicate that the corresponding service should be listening at the specified address for the specified protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: The general service-bitmap description and the set SMTP-bit example establish the advertised meaning; the service availability remains advisory.

requirements.quote:
The WKS record is used to describe the well known services supported by
a particular protocol on a particular internet address.  The PROTOCOL
field specifies an IP protocol number, and the bit map has one bit per
port of the specified protocol.  The first bit corresponds to port 0,
the second to port 1, etc.  If the bit map does not include a bit for a
protocol of interest, that bit is assumed zero.  The appropriate values
and mnemonics for ports and protocols are specified in [RFC-1010].

For example, if PROTOCOL=TCP (6), the 26th bit corresponds to TCP port
25 (SMTP).  If this bit is set, a SMTP server should be listening on TCP
port 25; if zero, SMTP service is not supported on the specified
address.
requirements.condition: When interpreting a zero WKS bitmap bit.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the zero bit as indicating that the corresponding service is not supported at the specified address for the specified protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: The general service-bitmap description and the zero SMTP-bit example establish the service-unavailable meaning.

requirements.quote:
The purpose of WKS RRs is to provide availability information for
servers for TCP and UDP.  If a server supports both TCP and UDP, or has
multiple Internet addresses, then multiple WKS RRs are used.
requirements.condition: When describing WKS availability for a server that supports both TCP and UDP.
requirements.required_behavior: Use multiple WKS resource records to describe the two protocols.
requirements.why_checkable: A dual-protocol server configuration can be checked for distinct WKS records covering its protocol-specific services.

requirements.quote:
The purpose of WKS RRs is to provide availability information for

multiple Internet addresses, then multiple WKS RRs are used.
requirements.condition: When describing WKS availability for a server with multiple Internet addresses.
requirements.required_behavior: Use multiple WKS resource records to describe the multiple addresses.
requirements.why_checkable: A multi-address server configuration can be checked for multiple address-specific WKS records.

requirements.quote: WKS RRs cause no additional section processing.
requirements.condition: When processing a WKS resource record.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Cause additional-section processing because of the WKS resource record.
requirements.why_checkable: The WKS response-building path can be checked for additional-section processing triggered by the WKS record.
